# Comwit UI — implementation guide

Comwit UI provides headless behavior (@comwit/ui) and editable component source installed into a React project by the comwit-ui CLI. It is a curated kit: for each job it wraps a proven library under a neutral name (page transitions on SSGOI, toasts on Sonner, popups on overlay-kit, springs on Motion, rich text on Tiptap, tables on TanStack Table, dates on React DayPicker, forms on React Hook Form) and installs the wrapper as source the project owns; the library itself is an npm dependency. The default look is the Comwit design system: warm white, deep ink, a blue brand (#3182f6), Pretendard, and refractive glass. It is independent of Comwit State.

## Install

Requires React 18 or 19. The styled templates use Tailwind CSS v4.

npx comwit-ui@latest init
npx comwit-ui@latest add button dialog input

Run these in the consumer project. init creates comwit.json, wires comwit-tokens.css, and installs base dependencies. add copies component sources and their registry dependencies (other components, lib/* and hooks/*), then installs needed npm dependencies. The default locations are components/ui, lib, and hooks; comwit.json controls aliases and the CSS path.

Import installed components from the consumer's configured alias, for example:

'use client'
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

Do not import @comwit/ui-templates in a CLI consumer app. It is the source package used to build the registry and previews. @comwit/ui remains a runtime dependency for behavior.

Put the font variable --font-pretendard on <html> (for example with next/font/local). Without it components fall back to the system font.

## Components

- Mobile app: app-bar, bottom-nav, page-transition (with route-boundary), pull-to-refresh, drag-scroller
- Glass: glass (Glass, GlassSurface, GlassButton), dropdown-menu, popover
- Notifications: toast (Toaster, toast(), Toast; formerly sonner), popup (popup.confirm / alert / sheet), alert, empty-state
- Pickers: date-picker, time-picker, month-picker (popover on desktop, bottom sheet on phones), calendar
- Selection: segmented-control, chip, checkbox, radio-group, pager
- Forms and data: text-field, autocomplete, select, form, data-table, editor
- Basics: button, badge, input, input-group, textarea, label, switch, tabs, accordion, collapsible, dialog, sheet, card, table, avatar, separator, skeleton, pagination

Dialog, sheet, popup and toast surfaces are refractive glass (the same material as menus and the app bar), denser over the modal scrim so text stays readable. Do not add bg-* classes to their content parts; that removes the glass.

## App shell

AppBar (behavior: flow | pinned | reveal) and BottomNav read one shared scroll intent. Wrap the scroller once:

import { ScrollChromeProvider } from '@/hooks/use-scroll-chrome'
<ScrollChromeProvider scrollRef={mainRef} resetKey={pathname}>…</ScrollChromeProvider>

Omit scrollRef to follow window scroll. PullToRefresh renders its own scroller and forwards ref to it, so pass that ref to ScrollChromeProvider. Routing is yours: pass onClick={() => router.back()} to AppBarBackButton or FloatingBackButton, and use BottomNavItem asChild with your Link.

## Page transitions

npx comwit-ui add page-transition

Installs components/ui/page-transition.tsx (PageTransition provider, generic PageBoundary, presets drill / sheet / slide / axis / zoom / hero / fade) and components/ui/route-boundary.tsx (RouteBoundary bound to the detected router: next, react-router or react-router-dom, @tanstack/react-router; otherwise a generic one that takes a path prop). Force one with --router nextjs|react-router|tanstack-router|generic. The engine (@ssgoi/react) is installed as a dependency; the copied files wrap it under these neutral names, so import from the copied files.

Mount the provider once around the routed region and mark that region with RouteBoundary. In Next.js this goes in app/layout.tsx around children:

'use client'
import { PageTransition, drill, sheet } from '@/components/ui/page-transition'
import { RouteBoundary } from '@/components/ui/route-boundary'

const transitions = {
  transitions: [
    { on: '/posts/**', except: '/posts', transition: drill() },
    { on: '/compose', transition: sheet({ type: 'blur' }) },
  ],
}

<PageTransition config={transitions}>
  <RouteBoundary>{children}</RouteBoundary>
</PageTransition>

PageTransition renders the shell the outgoing page needs (relative, z-0, min-h-dvh, overflow-x-clip); inside your own scroller pass className="min-h-full". Give every page a background. Persistent shells use an outer RouteBoundary with a fixed routeKey around an inner one. Without a router, PageBoundary takes path and routeKey directly. Reduced motion swaps pages without animating unless reducedMotion="keep".

Route rules (on/except, from/to, ordered, priority), every preset and its options, persistent layouts, scroll restoration and troubleshooting are SSGOI's and are documented at https://ssgoi.dev/llms.txt (config shape is identical; only the component names differ).

## Ownership

Edit copied component files directly. Existing files are skipped; --overwrite replaces local edits, so review first. Use --dry for a preview or --no-install when managing dependencies separately.

Keep behavior and accessibility in @comwit/ui; component source composes primitive parts and applies styles.

## Tokens

Use the shipped semantic utilities, not hardcoded colors:
- Surfaces and text: bg-background, bg-card, bg-muted, text-foreground, text-soft-foreground (default reading text), text-muted-foreground (meta), text-subtle-foreground (placeholder)
- Brand: bg-primary, hover:bg-primary-strong, bg-primary-surface with text-primary-ink
- Status (success, warning, destructive, info): bg-{s}, text-{s}-foreground, bg-{s}-surface, text-{s}-surface-foreground, border-{s}-border
- Radius: rounded-control (inputs), rounded-card, rounded-sheet, rounded-pill (buttons, chips); rounded-full is always a circle
- Type: text-display-xl…sm, text-title-lg…sm, text-body, text-body-sm, text-label, text-caption, text-micro
- Motion and layers: duration-fast/base/slow, z-appbar < z-overlay < z-modal < z-dropdown < z-toast
- Glass: the .glass material reads --glass-tint, --glass-opacity, --glass-edge, --glass-sheen, --glass-glow, --glass-shade and --glass-shadow; .glass-dense (dialogs, sheets, popups) tints with --popover at higher opacity

Theme by overriding primitives after the token import, for example :root { --brand: #0b68ba; --brand-strong: #08528f; --radius-scale: 0.6; --pill-radius: 12px }. Dark mode is the .dark class. There is no named-theme preset.

Always merge classes with cn() from lib/utils. It registers the token utilities with tailwind-merge; a plain twMerge silently drops text-label next to text-foreground and ring-focus next to ring-ring.

Keep a consumer's own global element rules (button, a, :focus-visible, h1–h3) inside @layer base. Unlayered element rules override Tailwind utilities and change the components' transitions, focus rings and fonts.

## Composition

Primitives use namespace exports such as Dialog.Root / Trigger / Portal / Overlay / Content / Title / Description / Close. Button, Input and Textarea are flat exports. Preserve labels, focus behavior and keyboard interactions when modifying a component. Use the actual component source for supported props; do not assume every shadcn or Radix API is interchangeable.

Default copy is English. Pickers take locale (Intl, for example 'ko-KR') and labels; Pager and DataTable take labels.

For direct unstyled use, install @comwit/ui and import primitives from that package. For styled UI, prefer the CLI installation flow above.

For imperative popup helpers mount OverlayProvider from overlay-kit once. For toast notifications install the toast template, mount its Toaster once, and call toast() from '@/components/ui/toast' (it renders the glass Toast component through sonner; sonner's own toast() would show sonner's default skin). Basic controls do not require these providers.
